citation: Detroit Publishing Co. 'The Pullman Residence, Chicago.' Glass negative no. 12551, between 1890 and 1901. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, Detroit Publishing Company Photograph Collection, LC-D4-12551; LC-DIG-det-4a08065.
author: Detroit Publishing Co.
date: between 1893 and 1901 (LOC: 1890-1901; the Fort Dearborn Massacre monument of 1893 is in the view)
repository: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division. The Prairie library holds the LOC derivative as a16-pullman-det-4a08065 in the image store (kevinrhaas/chicago-images).
locator: The whole print: the Pullman house at the north-east corner of Prairie Avenue and 18th Street, its west (Prairie) and south (18th Street) fronts.
rights_note: LOC: 'No known restrictions on publication.' A Detroit Publishing Co. photograph published before 1929.
access_notes: The image store's copy (a16-pullman-det-4a08065.jpg, 1024 x 804) fetched and viewed 2026-10-17; sha256 60140932328aa19142c1545028a1b2afee6767d3aff79cff3d98cd27cbc87d8c, matching the store's index.
note: The style library's Second Empire plate, and a building that stands in the 1904 scene (pullman_house_1729_prairie). It shows the three-storey stone block under a mansard roof crowned with iron cresting, with pedimented dormers and a columned porch. No source read names its style; the Landmarks report of 1973 describes its 'French-style mansard roof crowned with delicate and intricate ironwork', so the style is graded Inferred on the PHMC guide's features.
what_it_supplies: a public-domain view of the Pullman house about a decade before the 1904 scene date, showing its mansard, cresting and dormers
